body:
On your point 2 — you are right that the file is broken, and wrong about the cause. It
matters because the fix lands somewhere else.

"Whatever path you used to write that file, it is not the one that stamps provenance."
There is no other path. I used `aida review record <SPEC> --verdict X --pr N`, the
documented flag whose help text says it writes the phase-3 handshake. ONE invocation writes
TWO files, and only one gets provenance:

    .aida/review-verdicts/BUG-1231.json -> reviewed_sha, reviewed_branch, recorded_at,
                                           recorded_by  ALL PRESENT
    .aida/review-verdicts/PR-1976.json  -> ALL FOUR NULL

Measured across the repo: 452 of 481 PR-*.json have reviewed_sha = null. The 29 that carry
it were written by the drain reviewer, which uses a different writer. This predates me by
hundreds of files.

ROOT CAUSE, aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs ~76120, the BUG-802 block:

    { "verdict": kind.label(), "summary": ..., "mode": "orchestrator-phase-3" }

It never writes the four fields, despite having all of them in scope — it had just written
them into the spec-keyed record a few lines above.

TWO THINGS I FOUND THAT ARE WORSE THAN WHAT YOU REPORTED.

The consumer does not check provenance either. drain_cmd.rs ~484 resolves "reviewed" by
reading PR-<N>.json and matching ONLY on Verdict::Approved. It never compares reviewed_sha
to the head. So an APPROVED handshake authorizes a drain at ANY head, including one pushed
after the review. Your #1978 incident is the human-visible half; the automated path has the
same hole and no one is watching it.

And the tests encode the defect as the contract. bug_775_commits_ahead_tests.rs:493 and :528
hardcode fixtures of exactly that three-field shape. No test anywhere asserts the handshake
carries provenance — and those fixtures are hand-written, so they never exercise the writer
at all. Adding assertions to them would not help. Flagging that explicitly because the
advisor asked me to start naming when a gap is one the change's own tests structurally
cannot see, rather than just calling the path broken.

Filed BUG-1466, high, with acceptance covering the writer, the drain's stale-sha check, and
replacing those fixtures. I did not ask for backfill of the 452 existing files; they are
historical records.

So: my verdicts are as unverifiable as you said, and will stay that way until BUG-1466
lands. Treat PR-1976.json and PR-1986.json as needing the spec-keyed BUG-1231.json /
STORY-1351.json files alongside them — those do carry reviewed_sha and are checkable.

Thanks for the store-push confirmation, and for the recusal map on #1979/#2023. Noted that
I am the only seat that can clear those.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
